subject: Retroactive usage settlement + capacity purchase path (GridWorks)
messages:
From: Ava Dalton <ava.dalton@gridworks.io>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@gridworks.io
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Invoice 2026-11 Overage charge clarification

Hi Hiro,

We received the November invoice and there's a ~15% overage line item labeled "inference-hours: overage" for 11/2026 (invoice INV-2026-11-094). Can you send a breakdown of where the extra consumption came from? Our engineering team was not expecting a spike and we'd like to reconcile before processing payment.

Also: if this is billable, can you share options for smoothing the cost — we are preparing our Q1 forecast and would prefer a path that avoids a large one-time hit.

Thanks,
Ava Dalton
Head of CloudOps, GridWorks
Ava.Dalton@gridworks.io

Attachment: gridworks_nov_usage_summary.csv (CSV stub)

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Dalton <ava.dalton@gridworks.io>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, procurement@gridworks.io
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Invoice 2026-11 Overage charge clarification

Hi Ava — thanks for flagging this. I dug into the consumption and here are the quick findings: 

- Root cause: a misrouted canary job from a staging namespace was left on during the week of 11/10–11/14 and generated sustained high-concurrency streaming requests (approx +42% on that week).
- Impact: roughly 18k extra inference GPU hours (see attached CSV).

Options we can offer to mitigate the one-time impact:
1) One-time bridging credit: Redwood will apply a $45k credit to offset 60% of the overage while we cover the diagnostic hours. This appears to be a reasonable split given the staging origin.
2) Spread billing: we can amortize the remaining balance across Q1 invoices (3 equal installments) to lessen the immediate cashflow hit.
3) Capacity top-up + discount: if you commit to an incremental reserved block (6 months) we can discount that block and apply part of the discount to this overage.

If you prefer, we can combine 1) + 2). I'm looping in Marissa (accounts) to confirm internal approval and next steps for documentation/DocuSign.

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Enterprise Accounts — Redwood Inference
hiro.tanaka@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: settlement_terms_draft.pdf (PDF stub)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding GridWorks' note and my suggested mitigation (see settled terms draft attached). Quick asks:

- If yes, Marissa, will billing need a signed SOW / DocuSign amendment or is an email approval sufficient to issue credit?

Context: the spike originated from a staging canary that we own; still feels fair to share remediation. GridWorks is receptive to a combination of credit + spread billing and is open to a capacity top-up commitment if we offer a 12% discount on the incremental reserved block.

Thanks — I can join a quick 15-min call if helpful.

— Hiro

Thanks for the summary, Hiro — approve the plan with these caveats: 

- Apply the $45k credit against INV-2026-12 (we'll record as settlement credit).
- Amortize the residual balance over Jan–Mar 2027 invoices (3 equal installments).
- If GridWorks signs a 6-month incremental reserved block for +20% capacity, we extend a 12% discount and apply an additional $10k settlement credit upon signature.

Billing / Legal notes: we need a short amendment (one-page) capturing the credit and the amortization schedule. An email from procurement confirming acceptance is sufficient for billing to issue the credit, but Legal prefers DocuSign for the capacity commitment discount.

Marissa Cole
